05-contrast.title: Contrast is math, not taste.
05-contrast.alt: Accessibility card. Contrast is math, not taste. 4.5 : 1, Minimum contrast for body text, WCAG 2.2 AA. Try this: Check your muted text colour against its background in DevTools. The colour picker shows the ratio.
05-contrast.linkedin:
Contrast is math, not taste.

WCAG AA asks for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 for body text and 3 to 1 for large text. Light grey on white rarely makes it.

Try this today: Check your muted text colour against its background in DevTools. The colour picker shows the ratio.

07-nosniff.title: Stop browsers guessing file types.
07-nosniff.alt: Security card. Stop browsers guessing file types. Code: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Pairs well with correct Content-Type headers. Try this: Add it next to HSTS in the same rule, so both ship together.
07-nosniff.linkedin:
Stop browsers guessing file types.

11-hsts.title: One header. 180 days of HTTPS only.
11-hsts.alt: Security card. One header. 180 days of HTTPS only. Code: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=15552000. 15,552,000 seconds = 180 days. Try this: Run curl -sI on your domain and look for strict-transport-security. If it is missing, add it at your host or CDN.
11-hsts.linkedin:
One header. 180 days of HTTPS only.

HSTS tells browsers to never load your site over plain HTTP again. It takes one line of configuration on most hosts.

Try this today: Run curl -sI on your domain and look for strict-transport-security. If it is missing, add it at your host or CDN.

How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=tips-2026-10&utm_content=hsts

When the same content answers at several addresses, ranking signals split between them. Tell search engines which address is the real one.

Try this: Open your top page with and without a trailing slash and ?utm_ tags. Both should point to one canonical.
